correctness.rationale: Independent symbolic check: the map taking four subset coefficients to the linear combination of facet-area vectors has one-dimensional kernel generated by (1,1,1,1). It follows that nontrivial subsets give distinct nonzero axes except for complementary subsets (opposite orientation), so counting the four singleton and three pair-sum axes is legitimate. The support function is the maximum of the subset linear forms, hence only candidate vectors of maximum norm can give maximizing directions and each gives both signs. The sum of the three pair squared norms equals the sum of the four singleton squared norms; three maximal singletons would force the latter strictly above 3M^2. Equality needs precisely two singletons and all three pairs. Rescale and label the two singletons e,f; their pair norm forces e dot f=-1/2. Then t=||F_3||^2, ||F_4||^2=1-t, and e dot F_3=f dot F_3=-t/2, giving the stated decomposition along e+f and its common perpendicular. Conversely those vectors balance, span for precisely the open interval 0<t<1, and have the required norms; the discrete surface-area measure is admissible for Minkowski's theorem. At t=1/2 the five unit axes have maximum absolute off-diagonal dot product 3/4, checked by writing the last two as (e-f)/2 plus or minus g/2. The remaining candidate norms are 1/sqrt(2). The closest caps meet at their normalized bisector at height sqrt(7/8), with measure-zero boundary at contact, and overlap on an open set immediately below. Thus the union has probability 5(1-z) down to that sharp endpoint (or 5(1-z/M) on the rescaled interval). The proof is exact; the frozen checker was read, not executed.
